subject: OrchardTech x Redwood — revenue split model, lead-protection, and next steps
messages:
From: Jane Li <jane.li@orchardtech.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@orchardtech.com>, procurement@orchardtech.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Intro: OrchardTech x Redwood — revenue model + lead protection

Hi Sean / Laura,

Great chatting earlier this week. Attached is a short proposal that outlines the commercial starting point OrchardTech is comfortable with for a reseller + co-sell model (see Orchard_Redwood_Revshare_Proposal.pdf). High level:

- 20% revenue share on net ARR for Orchard-originated deals where Orchard owns the primary contract.
- 10% referral credit for Redwood-originated deals where Orchard provides implementation services and brings ongoing maintenance.
- 12-month claim window for lead registration with a 6-month acceleration/attribution rule if the opportunity enters POC with Orchard within 90 days.

We care about a clean lead-protection clause (no duplicate registration on the same account within 12 months) and a simple clawback for refunds/cancels within the first 90 days (pro rata).

Can you confirm Redwood’s standard accounting on net ARR and whether you’d accept the 12-month registration window? Also looping in Procurement for a heads-up on commercial terms.

Thanks — happy to sync next week for a 30-min alignment.

Best,
Jane Li
Partnerships Lead, OrchardTech
[jane.li@orchardtech.com]

Attachments: Orchard_Redwood_Revshare_Proposal.pdf
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro: OrchardTech x Redwood — revenue model + lead protection

Jane — thanks for the clear proposal and the PDF. Short answers up front:

- Net ARR: Redwood recognizes net ARR excluding taxes and platform credits; we treat one-time implementation fees separately (no share unless bundled into subscription).
- Registration window: 12 months is on the longer side for our standard playbook, but we can support it for strategic partners with a couple of guardrails (dedup process and demo/activity requirements).
- Clawback: pro rata refund within 90 days is reasonable. We typically track clawbacks at the invoice level.

Diego and Marissa — looping you both for ops/implementation detail. Can we get a cleaned rev-split spreadsheet (per-product SKU levels) and a proposed registration intake form for HubSpot? Jane — would you be able to share examples of Orchard’s registration confirmation email so we can validate the dedup logic?

I can take the contract-side commercial template and propose edits for the registration and clawback language. Shall we aim for a 30-min call on Tue 14th at 10am PT?

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Strategic Partnerships | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com

Sean / Team / Jane — I put together a first-draft revenue matrix (partner_revenue_matrix_v2.xlsx) to surface edge cases. Key notes: 

- Product SKUs: We need Orchard to indicate which SKUs they will resell vs. which are implementation-only. Commission % will vary by SKU (we used 20/12/8 buckets in the sheet).
- Registration flow: propose a required minimum qualification on the registration form — at least: company domain, estimated ARR, expected contract sign date, and stage (MQL / SQL / POC).
- Duplicate detection: HubSpot dedupe will be based on primary domain + normalized account name + Salesforce ID handshake for joint deals. If Orchard registers a single contact but Redwood has an active opp older than 12 months, we’d flag for manual review.

Open questions for Orchard:
1) If Orchard introduces a customer who signs twice (two separate legal entities under the same ultimate parent), do you expect separate credits?
2) Payment timing for commissions: net 30 after Redwood recognizes revenue or after customer payment receipt?

Thanks all — commercial ops input below and a suggested lightweight SLAs doc attached (Orchard_Docs_SLA-comments.pdf). Practical recommendations:

- Registration acceptance SLA: 48 business hours for automatic accept / reject. Manual escalations get 3 business days.
- Early-stage credits: Provide a provisional hold (30 days) while credit is confirmed; if credit is disputed, we open a joint review channel with both AMs and record a resolution in HubSpot.
- Commission payment: Redwood prefers net 30 after revenue recognition, but we can offer a net 45 option for partners that request consolidated monthly payments.
- Clawback mechanics: pro rata refund tracked as negative commission within the same fiscal quarter; original commission recouped from subsequent payouts if necessary.

I’ll prepare the HubSpot intake template and post a sample in the shared Drive folder. Jane — if Orchard wants faster payments we can discuss an invoice cadence in the contract.

—Marissa
Senior Partner Programs Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

- For parent/child legal entities: Orchard expects credits per legal entity unless we explicitly declare them as a consolidated account. We’ll include our company hierarchy export with the spreadsheet.
- Payment: Orchard prefers net 30 after revenue recognition.

1) Orchard sends populated revenue matrix + hierarchy export (EOD Wed 12/15).
2) Redwood publishes HubSpot intake template and draft contract redlines (Sean to send by 12/16).
3) Marissa to create registration SLA doc in Drive; Diego to enable dedupe rules in the staging environment.

Also scheduling: we confirmed Tue 12/21 10:00am PT for a 30-min commercial alignment (calendar invite to follow). I sent a draft DocuSign envelope for the NDA + commercial outline: https://docusign.net/envelope/0ABC123DEF
